Step 2: By submitting the rescission package with only 5 days left in the fiscal year, the White House structurally prevents Congress from acting before funds expire.
Step 3: A prior use of this tactic ($5B in foreign aid) was upheld 6-3 by the Supreme Court, providing partial legal precedent.

claims.claim_text: The collapse of China's implicit government guarantee on financial products — driven by Xi Jinping's centralization of power — has permanently destroyed credit demand and prevented any repeat of post-2008-style stimulus effectiveness.
reasoning_chain: Step 1: For decades, Chinese financial actors operated under an implicit assumption that the government would backstop losses on wealth management products, shadow banking instruments, and property developer debt.
Step 2: This guarantee was credible under collective CCP leadership because party weakness made political response to financial protests likely.

Step 3: Xi's centralization removed this dynamic: defaults on peer-to-peer lending (2018), smaller banks (2019), trust companies (2020), property developers (2021), individual mortgages (2022), and LGFVs (2023) were allowed to proceed without full compensation.
Step 4: A flight-to-quality replaced the historical flight-to-risk, causing credit demand to collapse structurally rather than cyclically.
Step 5: Authorities cannot credibly reinstate the implicit guarantee because Xi's governance model makes the threat of non-intervention credible, and market participants have been burned.
Step 6: This means future stimulus — even if large — cannot regenerate the same credit multiplier effects seen in 2009-2015, fundamentally capping China's recovery potential.
